Title: A new BDI agent architecture based on the belief theory. Application to the modelling of cropping plan decision-making
Reason: Explicit BDI agents for agricultural cropping-plan decisions; IC3/IC4 to confirm in full text.
Full_Text_Screening_Notes: The implemented study evaluates a BDI decision architecture for many farmer agents, but does not substantively model coordination, communication, cooperation, competition, negotiation, or shared-resource interaction among those agents. Coupling to the wider MAELIA system is described as subsequent work.

Title: Fine spatio-temporal simulation of cropping and farming systems effects on irrigation withdrawal dynamics within a river basin
Reason: MAELIA-related agricultural irrigation/farmer-agent study; likely related to SF13.
Full_Text_Screening_Notes: Meets the agricultural MAS criteria. Farmer agents make irrigation/cropping decisions within the MAELIA platform and are coupled to hydrological and normative components representing shared water availability and withdrawal restrictions. Likely related to the existing MAELIA study family.

Title: Agent-based spatial models applied to agriculture: a simulation tool for technology diffusion, resource use changes and policy analysis
Reason: Direct foundational agricultural MAS with farm-household interaction and resource-use feedback; eligible under IC7 foundational exception.
Full_Text_Screening_Notes: Meets the foundational-study exception (IC7) and substantive MAS criteria. Heterogeneous farm-household agents have explicit social/spatial interactions, technology diffusion, and irrigation/resource-use feedback in a peer-reviewed agricultural study.

Title: SHADOC: a multi-agent model to tackle viability of irrigated systems
Reason: Direct foundational multi-agent irrigation study with farmer organization/coordination; IC7 exception.
Full_Text_Screening_Notes: Meets IC7 foundational exception. SHADOC is an explicit agricultural multi-agent model centred on farmer organisation, coordination, social networks, water allocation, credit access, and irrigated-system viability.

Title: SINUSE: A multi-agent model to negotiate water demand management on a free access water table
Reason: Direct negotiation among irrigators over groundwater demand; IC7 foundational exception.
Full_Text_Screening_Notes: Meets IC7 foundational exception. SINUSE explicitly models irrigators, direct farmer interaction, shared groundwater dynamics, and negotiation/management interventions for an overexploited aquifer.

Title: Agent based simulation of a small catchment water management in northern Thailand: Description of the CATCHSCAPE model
Reason: Explicit agricultural water-management MAS with farmer decisions/interactions; IC7 foundational exception.
Full_Text_Screening_Notes: Meets IC7 foundational exception. CATCHSCAPE is an explicit agricultural/water-management MAS with farmer decisions, upstream–downstream conflict, negotiation, and shared catchment water/land/resource dynamics.

Title: Suitability of Multi-Agent Simulations to study irrigated system viability: application to case studies in the Senegal River Valley
Reason: Direct irrigated-system MAS with collective rules/interactions; IC7 foundational exception.
Full_Text_Screening_Notes: Meets IC7 foundational exception. The study uses a MAS virtual irrigated system with individual and collective rules and social dynamics to analyse irrigated-system viability in the Senegal River Valley; it is closely related to SHADOC.
